about: Defects seeded into sample 1 to measure what the audit's checks catch. Each is one edit of one file.

defects.what: A line's quantity can be changed to less than what has already shipped: the check is gone.
An order can be cancelled as a whole although something on it has shipped.
A shipment that closes the last open line no longer re-derives the order: it stays CONFIRMED.
Cancelling an order cancels its lines but leaves their planned deliveries planned.

defects.what: The event is recorded in a transaction of its own, so it stays when the change it describes is rolled back.
Committing a change answers as if it had succeeded when it failed for a reason that is not a business refusal; nothing was changed.
defects.note: The first version of this defect swallowed a failure to record the event while confirming an order. It changed nothing observable: the framework marks the transaction for rollback once the write fails, so the order was not confirmed either way. No check noticed it, rightly; it was replaced.

defects.what: Confirming an order publishes its event directly, before the transaction commits.
An applied shipment message is no longer remembered, so its id does not protect against anything.

defects.what: The preview of cancelling a line skips the checks: it shows a result where proposing and committing refuse.
The preview reports the change of amount with the wrong sign; what is committed is right.
The order total counts cancelled lines too.
A shipment adds the whole line's quantity to what has shipped, not the delivery's.

defects.what: Reading an order shows a line's quantity and shipped quantity swapped; the stored data is right.
Confirming and cancelling an order no longer lock it: two of them at once both read the order as it was.
Applying a shipment no longer locks the order: two shipments of the same line at once both read it as it was.
